blocks.intro: Many Mokena homes built in the 1990s and 2000s came with a gas fireplace.

items.body: Most are sealed units that vent through the wall. Parts are usually available, so repairs are straightforward.
Thermocouples, igniters and gaskets wear out. A yearly service catches them early.
Every home with a gas fireplace should have a working detector near the bedrooms and on every floor.
If the fireplace won't respond to the remote or switch, the receiver batteries or the wiring are often the cause, not the gas valve.

blocks.h2: Gas Fireplace Questions From Mokena Homeowners

items.q: Why won't my gas fireplace pilot stay lit?
items.preview: Usually a dirty pilot or a weak thermocouple.
items.answer: Usually the pilot is dirty or the thermocouple or thermopile is weak. Cleaning or replacing the part fixes it.

items.q: How often should a gas fireplace be serviced?
items.preview: Once a year, before the heating season.
items.answer: Once a year, ideally in early fall, so problems are found before the first cold night.

items.q: Can you clean the glass on my fireplace?
items.answer: Yes. We clean the glass as part of a yearly service and check the gasket that seals it.

items.preview: We run the gas line and connect it.
items.answer: We run and test the gas line and connect the unit. For framing and venting through the wall, we'll coordinate with the installer.

items.q: My fireplace clicks but won't light. What's wrong?
items.preview: Usually the igniter, the pilot or the battery backup.
items.answer: On many direct-vent units, it's a weak igniter, a dirty pilot assembly or dead batteries in the receiver or backup. We test each one.

items.q: How much does gas fireplace repair cost in Mokena?
items.preview: It depends on the part and the fireplace. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what failed and the type of fireplace. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
